open_points.subject: startup recovery of a run with both ready and waiting elements
open_points.text: “A run derived `running` is advanced with `runs`' own advance, which reaches every ready element while other elements still wait …; a run derived still waiting is not advanced” conflicts with M19’s rule that a run’s status is `awaiting_approval` when any element waits for approval and otherwise `pending`, without stating whether readiness takes precedence during recovery.
open_points.question: When recovery finds at least one ready element and at least one element that still waits, must `run_graph` derive `running` so `runs` advances the ready elements, or derive the waiting status and perform no advance?
options: Derive `running` whenever any element is ready, advance until no ready element remains, then persist `awaiting_approval` or `pending`.
Derive `awaiting_approval` or `pending` whenever any wait exists and do not advance other ready elements during recovery.
open_points.default_guess: Derive `running` and advance all ready work before persisting the remaining waiting state, following A13 rule 8.
